q: Match each definition with the gestation or weight it uses — 1) Abortion 2) WHO definition of abortion 3) Intrauterine death … A) Fetal weight below 500 g, about 22 weeks B) Pregnancy loss at or after 20 weeks C) Pregnancy loss before 20 weeks
exp: Abortion is pregnancy loss before 20 weeks; the WHO definition is fetal weight below 500 g, about 22 weeks; and intrauterine death is loss at or after 20 weeks.

q: Fill up: The WHO definition of abortion is a fetal weight below ______ g, approximately below ______ weeks.
exp: The WHO definition uses a fetal weight below 500 g, approximately 22 weeks.

q: Fill up: Abortion is pregnancy loss before ______ weeks, whereas intrauterine death is loss at or after ______ weeks.
exp: Abortion is pregnancy loss before 20 weeks of gestation, and intrauterine death is pregnancy loss at or after 20 weeks.

q: Which statement about the period of viability is TRUE?
opts: The notes state a period of viability of 28 weeks in India
The notes state a period of viability of 24 weeks in India
The source definition puts viability at 32 weeks
Viability is reached at 20 weeks in the source notes
exp: The notes state a period of viability of 28 weeks in India.

q: Fill up: Spontaneous abortion is subdivided into an ______ single episode or ______ abortion.
opts: Recurrent; isolated, meaning a single loss
exp: In the source flowchart spontaneous abortion is subdivided into an isolated single episode and recurrent abortion with at least 3 abortions.

q: Fill up: An abortion that is induced medically is termed ______.
exp: Induced abortion is medical termination of pregnancy.

q: A woman who had a surgical evacuation four days ago now has fever, lower abdominal pain and an offensive vaginal discharge, and her os is open. Which feature makes this a septic abortion?
opts: The presence of septic foci in association with the abortion
Rh negativity of the mother on its own
An open internal os by itself, without any infection
Fetal cardiac activity still seen on the scan
exp: Any abortion with septic foci is a septic abortion; neither Rh negativity, an open os alone nor fetal cardiac activity defines it.

q: A 30-year-old woman has a single isolated first-trimester pregnancy loss. She has no history of thrombosis, no cervical surgery and no systemic disease. What is the most common cause of this kind of loss?
exp: Chromosomal anomaly is the most common cause of an isolated first- or second-trimester abortion, and aneuploidy is the most common category.

q: Which statement about chromosomal anomalies in isolated abortion is TRUE?
opts: Aneuploidy is the most common category
Balanced translocation is the most common category
Triploidy accounts for most isolated abortions
Mitochondrial mutations are the leading category
exp: Aneuploidy is listed as the most common chromosomal anomaly in isolated abortion.

q: All of the following are listed chromosomal abnormalities in isolated abortion EXCEPT:
exp: The source order is aneuploidy, then trisomy, then monosomy (Turner syndrome), then trisomy 16; a mitochondrial mutation is not listed.

q: All of the following are listed causes or risk factors for isolated abortion EXCEPT:
exp: Listed risk factors are a previous abortion and increasing maternal age, with chromosomal anomaly the commonest cause; daily walking is not a risk factor.

q: Which statement about maternal age and isolated abortion is TRUE?
opts: The risk of isolated abortion increases with maternal age
Maternal age has no effect on the risk of isolated abortion
Only paternal age affects the risk of isolated abortion
The risk falls to zero after the age of 35 years
exp: Increasing maternal age is a listed risk factor for isolated abortion.

q: Which statement about infection and recurrent abortion is TRUE?
opts: Infections do not cause recurrent abortion
All infections are the commonest cause of recurrent abortion
TORCH serology always proves a diagnosis of recurrent abortion
VDRL testing is mandatory in every case of recurrent loss
exp: The notes state that infections do not cause recurrent abortion.

q: Fill up: In congenital syphilis the pregnancy prognosis follows ______ law, improving as the number of pregnancies ______.
exp: Kassowitz law states that the pregnancy prognosis is proportional to the number of pregnancies in syphilis; stillbirth is more common than abortion.

q: Fill up: The most lethal trisomy is trisomy ______, while the most viable is trisomy ______.
exp: Trisomy 16 is the most lethal in the note, and trisomy 21 is the most viable, with abortion its most common outcome.

q: A 38-year-old woman has a second-trimester loss and products of conception are sent for karyotyping, which returns trisomy 21. How is this trisomy described in the notes?
opts: The most viable, with abortion as its commonest outcome
The most lethal of all the autosomal trisomies
Incompatible with implantation, so never seen in losses
Always inherited from a parental balanced translocation
exp: Trisomy 21 is the most viable trisomy and abortion is its most common outcome; trisomy 16 is the most lethal.

q: Which statement about HIV and pregnancy loss is TRUE?
opts: HIV is neither abortogenic nor teratogenic
HIV is abortogenic but not teratogenic
HIV is teratogenic but not abortogenic
HIV is always both abortogenic and teratogenic
exp: The source explicitly states that HIV is neither abortogenic nor teratogenic.

q: Fill up: Recurrent abortion is defined as at least ______ consecutive pregnancy losses before ______ weeks.
exp: Recurrent abortion is at least 3 consecutive pregnancy losses before 20 weeks.

q: Match the delivery plan in eclampsia with what the source says about it — 1) Mode generally preferred 2) Caesarean section 3) Anaesthesia written for delivery … A) General anaesthesia B) Only for an obstetric indication C) Vaginal delivery
exp: After stabilisation vaginal delivery is generally preferred, caesarean is indicated only for an obstetric indication, and the p402 note lists general anaesthesia.

q: Fill up: In eclampsia, caesarean section is indicated ______.
opts: In every woman who has had a seizure
On the basis of proteinuria alone
exp: Cesarean section is indicated only for an obstetric indication, not merely because a seizure has occurred.

q: Which statement about anaesthesia for delivery in eclampsia is TRUE?
opts: The p402 eclampsia delivery note lists general anaesthesia
Spinal anaesthesia is mandatory in every case of eclampsia
No anaesthesia should be given during delivery in eclampsia
Local perineal infiltration alone is the recommended technique
exp: The p402 eclampsia delivery note lists general anaesthesia.

q: Fill up: Impending eclampsia is seen in patients with ______ pre-eclampsia.
exp: Impending eclampsia is seen in patients with severe pre-eclampsia.

q: Fill up: The commonest warning symptom of impending eclampsia is a severe ______, present in about ______ of cases.
exp: Severe headache is the most common stated symptom of impending eclampsia, occurring in about 70%.

q: All of the following are recognised features of impending eclampsia EXCEPT:
exp: Impending eclampsia features severe headache, epigastric pain from subcapsular hematoma and visual disturbances; painless vaginal bleeding suggests placenta previa instead.

q: A woman with severe pre-eclampsia at 32 weeks develops a severe headache and epigastric pain, and her blood pressure is 170/115 mmHg. What is the correct sequence of management?
opts: Magnesium sulfate, then antihypertensives, then delivery once stabilised
Immediate caesarean section before any anticonvulsant is given
Salt restriction and bed rest, with delivery planned at 36 weeks
Insulin and fetal echocardiography, with delivery left until term
exp: MgSO4 prevents seizures, antihypertensives treat the blood pressure, and the pregnancy is terminated after stabilisation regardless of gestation.

q: All of the following are recognised visual disturbances of pre-eclampsia EXCEPT:
exp: Blurred vision, scotoma, diplopia and blindness are the listed visual disturbances; hearing loss is not one of them.

q: Fill up: Blindness is listed in about ______ of severe pre-eclampsia cases.
exp: Blindness is listed in 10-15% of severe pre-eclampsia cases.

q: All of the following are listed causes of visual loss in severe pre-eclampsia EXCEPT:
exp: Listed causes are occipital blindness, retinal artery occlusion and retinal detachment; cataract is not among them.

q: Which statement about blindness in severe pre-eclampsia is TRUE?
opts: It is usually reversible, except with retinal artery occlusion or detachment
It is always permanent once vision has been lost
It never occurs in severe pre-eclampsia
It is unrelated to pregnancy and needs no specific care
exp: Blindness in severe PE is usually reversible; retinal-artery occlusion or retinal detachment are listed exceptions to reversibility.

q: Match the visual-loss term with what it refers to — 1) Amaurosis fugax 2) Purtscher retinopathy 3) Hypertensive retinopathy classification … A) Retinal infarction B) Occipital blindness C) Keith-Wagener classification
exp: Occipital blindness is labelled amaurosis fugax, retinal infarction is termed Purtscher retinopathy, and hypertensive retinopathy uses the Keith-Wagener classification.

q: Fill up: Hypertensive retinopathy is classified by the ______ classification.
exp: Hypertensive retinopathy is classified by the Keith-Wagener classification.

q: A woman has an eclamptic seizure and the team has secured her airway and is controlling the fits. What should be checked first, and what must be ruled out if fetal distress persists?
opts: Fetal heart sound first, then rule out abruptio placentae
Fetal blood group first, then rule out gestational diabetes
Amniotic fluid bile acids first, then rule out thyroid storm
Maternal HbA1c first, then rule out cervical incompetence
exp: The stepwise algorithm first checks the fetal heart sound; with persistent fetal distress the source directs clinicians to rule out abruptio placentae and consider caesarean.
